vulnerabilityReview.rationale: Reviewed by the sole maintainer for Hospital 1.2.3 on 2026-08-31 and accepted on provenance grounds. This is not an inheritance and is not claimed as one: the reviewed-inputs fingerprint moved, so the 1.2.2 acceptance could not carry forward. Two facts were checked rather than assumed. First, no source component changed -- PostgreSQL 17.11, zlib 1.3.2 and ACL 2.4.0 keep the same versions, the same source URLs and the same SHA-256 checksums, and the Debian snapshot, the configure flags and the embedded build records are unchanged; no Dockerfile and no file under infra/docker was modified, so nothing that compiles, links or selects these components moved. Second, what did move is the pinned image set alone, which the fingerprint now covers: node:24-alpine3.24, postgres:17.11-bookworm and golang:1.26.6-alpine3.24 were re-resolved to current upstream digests of the same tags, and the Trivy scanner moved from 0.73.0 to 0.74.0. Those four changes are accepted on provenance grounds -- identical tags with re-resolved digests, and a scanner minor upgrade -- without a fresh CVE review of the rebuilt base images. Unlike 1.2.2, this release does change two files under infra/postgres, backup-once.sh and restore.sh; both are runtime backup and restore logic and neither participates in building or linking the source components. The 1.1.0 findings are carried forward, not re-verified, and are now twelve days old: that PostgreSQL 17.11, released 2026-08-13, was then the newest 17.x security release; that zlib 1.3.2, released 2026-02-17, was the newest upstream release, and that CVE-2026-22184 does not apply to it because that flaw affects the untgz contrib utility through 1.3.1.2, which 1.3.2 removed; and that ACL 2.4.0 falls outside the affected ranges for CVE-2026-54369 and CVE-2026-54370. This acceptance remains limited to the recorded checksums and provenance, because Trivy does not vulnerability-map these source-built components. The recorded fingerprint covers the components, the Debian snapshot, the configure flags, the embedded build records and the pinned images, so any later change to any of them forces a fresh review rather than another carry-forward.
